edge_cases: Missing required form fields result in a server error or unexpected response.
Attempting to register with an existing username returns "Username already exists".
Login with incorrect password or non‑existent username returns "Invalid credentials".
Creating a project for a non‑existent user returns "User not found".
Adding a task to a non‑existent project returns "Project not found".
SQL injection is possible due to string concatenation in queries.
contract.intent: Provide a simple web API for user registration, authentication, project creation, task management, and task viewing in a project management system.
invariants: Usernames must be unique; duplicate registration attempts are rejected.
Passwords are stored only as bcrypt hashes, never in plain text.
A project can be created only for an existing username.
A task can be added only to an existing project.
All database connections are closed after each request.
io_behavior: POST /register with form fields username, password, confirm_password returns a success or error message.
POST /login with form fields username, password redirects to /dashboard on success or returns "Invalid credentials".
POST /create_project with form fields project_name, description, username creates a project record and returns a status message.
POST /add_task with form fields project_name, task_name, task_description adds a task to an existing project and returns a status message.
GET /view_tasks?project_name=... returns a JSON array of tasks for the specified project.
side_effects: Inserts new rows into the users table on successful registration.
Inserts new rows into the projects table on successful project creation.
Inserts new rows into the tasks table on successful task addition.
Commits or rolls back database transactions based on operation outcome.
Issues an HTTP redirect to /dashboard after a successful login.

rationale: Core API endpoints and main functionality are implemented and respect most invariants and side‑effects, but error messages for missing user/project differ from the contract and the program prevents SQL injection, contradicting the specified edge‑case vulnerability.
